audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was scored as a Karma row on both layers while the why on that same row says Infinite Duress ends you, and the matchup was labelled EVEN 5.5/10 against a 30.77% win rate.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Karma, Skill, Warwick, Warwick, Warwick, Warwick, Warwick. Level 6 is Warwick's single hardest spike, so it cannot be Karma's row.
audit.corrected: Row 4 flipped to Warwick on both layers; difficulty raised to 8/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phase whys were generic Karma boilerplate that claimed she owns levels 4-5 and level 6.
audit.why: Warwick's spikes are Blood Hunt coming online (80s at rank 1, dropping to 40s), level 6 Infinite Duress (110/90/70s), and BORK plus Eternal Hunger at first item. Karma has no level-6 spike.
audit.corrected: Rewrote phases[0..6].why against those spikes with real cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer describes Infinite Duress as 'a point-and-click suppress' in three places. It is not point-and-click.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Warwick leaps in a direction (scaling with his bonus Move Speed), suppressing the first champion he collides with for 1.5 seconds.' It is a skillshot leap that hits the first champion in its path, and the kit flags it as a channel that any CC cancels. Calling it point-and-click tells a paying user there is nothing to dodge and no way to interrupt it — both false.
audit.corrected: Restated as a leap that suppresses the first champion collided with for 1.5s, with CC cancelling the channel. Also corrected 'ignores your E shield' — a shield never stops CC, that is not a Warwick-specific property.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal was a trailing clause and nothing warned against armour.
audit.why: Jaws of the Beast deals damage based on the target's maximum health and heals him for it, and Eternal Hunger triples its healing below 25% HP — so stacking resistances reads the trade wrong and Grievous Wounds timing decides every extended trade.
audit.corrected: Added both to breakdown.cooldowns where the sequencing advice lives.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flagged 'Blood Hunt's' and 'Gathering Fire's' as probable wrong names.
audit.why: Both false positives — possessive forms of Warwick's real W and Karma's real passive.

edits.before: Even matchup — difficulty 5.5/10, Warwick carry threat 6/10.
edits.after: Hard matchup — difficulty 8/10, Warwick carry threat 7.5/10.

edits.before: Q poke at level 1 is among the best in the game — chunk Warwick on every last-hit and start the Mantra economy.
edits.after: Mantra is up from level 1 — RQ Soulflare lands before Blood Hunt speed or Eternal Hunger sustain exist.

edits.before: W tether threatens the root — anyone who steps to you early eats Q-W and donates the trade.
edits.after: It evens fast — Blood Hunt speed and his Eternal Hunger drain start eating your chip as you trade.

edits.before: Full kit: E shield-speed makes you untouchable in short trades. Mantra-Q (RQ) on cooldown gaps is a third of his HP.
edits.after: Eternal Hunger heals harder the lower his HP gets, so once he is sustaining your poke refunds him faster than it hurts.

edits.before: Spam the RQ slow-field on his farming spots and keep your shield for Infinite Duress — the lane is a toll booth and you own it.
edits.after: Q and RQ rotations can't push him off the wave — Blood Hunt walks through the cooldown gaps and his drain heals the rest.

edits.before: No new ultimate at 6 — your Mantra has been online since level 1. His spike is the danger window: respect it.
edits.after: Infinite Duress suppresses for 1.5 seconds and no shield stops CC — alone, you die inside it. This is his spike.

edits.before: First item amplifies the RQ chunk — keep him under 60% and the lane stays yours by default.
edits.after: BORK plus Eternal Hunger out-heals your first AP spike, and Blood Hunt chases you down.

edits.before: You drift toward utility now — peel, shield, and speed your carries while the RQ poke softens objectives.
edits.after: He has drain-tank scaling and you have none — Blood Hunt catches you and low-HP heal turns your burst into sustain.

edits.before: His dash beats your poke rhythm — shield the engage, root the exit, and respect the all-in windows.
edits.after: Your poke feeds his drain — win level 1, then stop trading and never be caught alone at 6.

edits.before: Tax the approach, survive the dive, and grind him down between windows. Shorthand: Infinite Duress down, wave right, go.
edits.after: Bank level 1, then play for the map. Infinite Duress is 110s at rank 1 — that downtime is your only safe window.

edits.before: - Warwick Infinite Duress: matchup-defining — Lock-on suppress — track it before every step-up. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your E shield like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Infinite Duress: 110s at rank 1, 70s at rank 3 — a leap that suppresses for 1.5s, and any CC cancels the channel. - Q Jaws is max-health damage, so armour is the wrong buy: bring anti-heal. - Hold E for his all-in, never for poke.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is a point-and-click suppress that ignores your E shield and breaks your W tether — once it lands your thin frame dies before RE casts.
edits.after: Infinite Duress leaps and suppresses the first champion it hits for 1.5s — CC cancels the channel, but alone your frame dies before RE casts.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is a point-and-click suppress that ignores your E shield and breaks your W tether — once it locks you, you're dead before you can RE ripple out or your root lands.
edits.after: Infinite Duress is a 1.5s suppress on the first champion his leap collides with — a shield does not stop CC, so if you are alone you die before the RE ripple or your root lands.

edits.before: This is where it slips away. At 4-5 you want Inner Flame and RQ rotations to bully, but Blood Hunt's move speed walks through every poke gap and his Eternal Hunger + BORK heal it all back, so you can't actually push him off the wave. At 6 Infinite Duress is the lane-ender: it's a point-and-click suppress that your E shield can't absorb and that breaks your W tether mid-channel, and once it locks you, your thin frame is gone before the RE ripple even casts. Hold E and the root purely to survive the all-in, never to trade — bait nothing, just don't die to the suppress.

notes: The 'point-and-click suppress' line was the worst error in this matchup — Infinite Duress is a directional leap onto the first champion it collides with, and the kit flags it as an interruptible channel, so it is both dodgeable and cancellable by CC. Fixed in whys[4], spikes[1].text and mid. QA: tone is still the EVEN colour '#e8b84b' after diff moved to HARD; I left colour tokens alone since I have no verified tier mapping.
